aiMessage: I've known Stephen for a few years through work contacts, we were on friendly terms. I went over to his flat that evening to check on him, see how he was doing. I arrived around 22:41, we talked for maybe twenty minutes — just casual conversation. I left before half past eleven, walked back to my car, and drove home. I was back at my place by 23:24. I had no idea anything had happened until you lot called me.

detectiveInput: PRESENT e4: What do you mean by you were on friendly terms? Did the 21K loan affect your relationship somehow?

PRESENT e4: What do you mean by you were on friendly terms? Did the 21K loan affect your relationship somehow?
aiMessage: Look, yes, Stephen owed me money. A lot of money. But that doesn't mean we weren't friendly — we were. He was going through a rough patch financially, and I was helping him out. When I went over that night, I wasn't there to threaten him or anything like that. We talked about it, sure, but it was... it was civil. He said he'd sort it out, and I believed him. I left on good terms. I had no reason to hurt him — if anything, I needed him alive to pay me back.

aiMessage: Look, I've already said I left before half past. The drive from his flat to mine takes about... maybe eight, nine minutes depending on traffic. It was late, so there wasn't much traffic. I left around 23:15, give or take a couple of minutes. I'm not going to pretend I checked my watch when I walked out the door — I was upset, thinking about what he said. But yeah, that timing makes sense. I was home by 23:24, and that fits.

I wasn't there when it happened. I left, went home. I'm not hiding anything.

Why do you keep asking me these questions as if I did something? I'm grieving too, you know. I came here to help find out what happened to him.

detectiveInput: What happened on that night? And what was the weirdist thing you observed?

aiMessage: Well, I heard shouting coming from Stephen's flat upstairs that evening — two people going at it, you know. I'd taken my hearing aids out because it was getting loud, so I couldn't make out what they were saying, but it was definitely heated. Later on, around 23:03, I heard a door slam quite loudly. As for the weirdest thing — I suppose it was the shouting itself, really. Stephen usually kept to himself, quiet sort of chap. That's all I can tell you, I'm afraid.
